items.name: ICO AI & Data Protection Guidance
items.description: ICO guidance on AI and data protection: DPIAs, automated decision-making, transparency and bias, applied to AI systems that process personal data

requirements.text: Organisations using AI systems that process personal data conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments to identify and mitigate data protection risks before deploying the system.
requirements.rationale: A DPIA is the trigger point where AI data-protection risk must be confronted, per UK GDPR Article 35.

controls.description: Complete and file a DPIA for every AI system processing personal data before first use; refresh it on material change.

requirements.text: AI systems making or informing automated individual decisions comply with UK GDPR provisions on automated decision-making, including the right to human review and meaningful information about the logic involved.
requirements.rationale: Individual rights attach to consequential automated decisions regardless of the technique behind them.

controls.description: Provide a human-review route and a meaningful logic explanation for solely automated decisions affecting individuals.

requirements.text: Organisations are transparent about the use of AI in processing personal data, giving data subjects clear information about automated decision-making at the point of collection.
requirements.rationale: Transparency obligations are not diluted by the complexity of the underlying model.

controls.description: Update privacy notices to name AI processing purposes and automated decision logic in plain language.

requirements.text: AI systems processing personal data are designed and operated to avoid bias and ensure fair treatment, consistent with data protection principles.
requirements.rationale: Biased outputs can be inaccurate or unfairly discriminatory under data protection law.

controls.description: Assess training data and outputs for bias against protected characteristics and document mitigations.
